messages:
Morgan: Observing a spike in p50/p95 for 8-GPU runs after yesterday's runtime tweak. Looks like comm latency climbed. :eyes:
Sam: Which job? CI or prod?
Morgan: Prod inference cluster, dedicated pools. Model: redwood-7b, TP=2, PP=2, 4 nodes x 2 GPUs (NVLink internal, PCIe between hosts via EFA).
Tara: Any perf traces? pprof / nvprof?
Morgan: Yes — ran our lightweight tracer and an allreduce micro. Short excerpt: 
```
allreduce: count=512k tokens, avg_latency=1.2ms -> 3.9ms (per step)
compute_kernels: avg_step=12.3ms unchanged
comm_overlap: dropped from ~45% -> ~10%
```
Kevin: That jump is huge. Does kernel selection change cause smaller matmuls/increased launches?
Morgan: We also changed the kernel selector heuristics yesterday to prefer int8 GEMM for attention on short sequences. That reduced host-side CPU prep but I suspect fragmentation of large tensors -> more small async transfers.
Ivan: Can you paste the NCCL/ibverbs counters? Are we seeing more small messages on IB/EFA?
Morgan: From host NIC stats: cumulative small pkts (<4K) increased 3x. NCCL report shows many tiny allreduce segments: 128KB chunks instead of 4MB.
Priya: Sounds like topology-aware chunking broke. We used a heuristic that splits by local GPU memory boundaries; maybe on NVLink groups it should keep larger chunks.
Sam: If chunk size falls below rendezvous threshold, latency blows up. We saw this in a perf run when kernel-tiling changed tensor shapes.
Tara: Actionable experiments: (1) force single chunk allreduce on 8 GPUs; (2) revert kernel selector to previous thresholds; (3) run with NCCL_PROXY (intra-node only) to verify NVLink vs EFA diff.
Kevin: I can run (1) and (3) on canary pool. Command I used before: 
```bash
NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_BUFFSIZE=4194304 ./run_infer --model redwood-7b --gpus 8 --tp 2 --pp 2 --trace-allreduce
```
Morgan: I ran a quick compare: 
```
baseline (old selector): allreduce=1.1ms, overlap=48%
new selector: allreduce=3.8ms, overlap=12%
nvlink-only (node pin): allreduce=1.3ms
cross-node (EFA path): allreduce=3.6ms
```
Ivan: That points to chunking hitting cross-node path too often. Maybe our routing tried to split tensors across device-groups instead of keeping within NVLink islands.
Priya: We recently landed a change to the placer that tries to maximize per-device memory locality; it may be interleaving shards across nodes when combined with TP stripe. I'll open a PR to revert the placement heuristic for the canary.
Sam: Also check our KV cache batching heuristics — if requests with different prefixes are batched, the cache miss pattern can create lots of small kv updates spread over all GPUs.
Morgan: Good call. I saw KV write amplification: small KV writes per step up 2.5x. That would explain more cross-device chatter.
Tara: Quick repro plan for today: run these permutations and collect per-step NCCL timeline + kernel launch counts + kv write sizes. Use the profiler wrapper: 
```bash
./profiler --job=redwood-7b --nodes=4 --gpus-per-node=2 --collect=nccL,timeline,kv --out=/tmp/run1
```
Kevin: I'll queue runs on canary and tag results. If we confirm chunking is the cause, short-term mitigations: increase NCCL_BUFFSIZE, force larger chunking in our allreduce wrapper, or adjust kernel selector to prefer shapes that lead to larger continuous buffers.
Morgan: Can someone own correlating kernel selection changes to buffer tiling? I can own the KV batching angle.
Priya: I'll take the placer revert and run cluster-level canary.
Ivan: I'll instrument NCCL to dump message sizes for the failing runs. perf-bot: queued run 1769054330 for canary pool (owner: Kevin).
perf-bot: aggregated trace ready: /artifacts/1769054330/nccl_trace.txt
Kevin: Trace shows ~75% of cross-node messages are <=128KB after the selector change. Before it was mostly >=1MB.
Sam: That matches the increased latency — many small roundtrips + serialization overhead on EFA.
Tara: Longer-term: the placer and kernel selector need a topology-aware contract. Kernel selector should expose preferred chunk alignments or min contiguous bytes per replica so comm layer can keep chunking aligned to NVLink islands.
Priya: Agreed. I'll add an interface: kernel_selector.provide_comm_hints({"min_chunk": 1<<20, "prefer_local_groups": true})
Morgan: For immediate rollback, we should flip the selector heuristic and redeploy canary. deploy-bot: scheduled rollback to prev-kernel-selector at 1769054380 (canary only).
deploy-bot: rollback complete on canary, monitoring metrics.
Morgan: After rollback, preliminary numbers: allreduce back to ~1.2ms, overlap ~46%, KV writes normalized. Looking better.
Kevin: Great. Next steps: define invariants and tests to catch regressions: add an integration e2e perf test that simulates mixed-prefix KV loads + multi-node NVLink/EFA topology and fails CI if avg allreduce > 2ms for 8-GPU redwood-7b.
Sam: I'll draft the CI test and failure thresholds. We should also add perf assertions to PRs changing kernel selection or placer.
Tara: Thanks team — good rapid debug loop. Let's keep traces for a week in case any drift. :thumbsup:
